title: THE SEVEN TRUMPETS
mv: And I saw the seven angels who stand before God, and to them were given seven trumpets.
mvp: “And I saw the seven angels who stand before God, and to them were given seven trumpets.” Revelation 8:2 (NKJV)
assignment: Mention two (2) reasons for the blowing of the trumpets (5x2=10 Marks).

b.x: The Seven Trumpets of the book of Revelation are a sequence of apocalyptic events detailed in Revelation chapters 8 to 11. They are introduced following the opening of the seventh seal. These trumpet judgements are components of the broader vision revealed to the Apostle John. Each trumpet symbolises a divine punishment unleashed on the earth throughout the Great Tribulation. As the trumpets sound, their severity escalates, serving as warnings, executing judgement, and heralding the arrival of God’s kingdom.
The seven trumpets would be blown to:

i: Serve as a call to repentance (Acts 3:19).
Prepare for the final establishment of God's kingdom (Revelation 11:15; 12:10).

b.x: The Seven Trumpets of the book of Revelation are more than just events yet to come; they demonstrate God’s patience, justice, and authority, encouraging humanity to repent and prepare for Christ’s return (Revelation 2:7).

i: What do you understand by the seven trumpets?
Briefly describe the content of the fifth and sixth trumpets.
